column3: The Hebrew repeats “the inhabitants” before Sidon.
The Hebrew uses singular collective names for the Asherite and the Canaanite.
The Hebrew keeps Naphtali as an unnamed singular subject of dwelling rather than naming the Naphtalites.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite” and a singular object pronoun for Dan.
The Hebrew preserves the image of the hand of Joseph’s house becoming heavy; BSB describes Joseph’s house growing in strength and pressing the Amorites into labor.
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite” and ends “from the rock and upward.”
